agree.reason: The 3 a.m. solo shift, two missed shifts and nine early mastitis catches make a believable case, but bracket placeholders and no concrete payoff or support plan leave a quick reader with no strong reason to rank this letter above the other 149.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented, and the claims stay close to the brief, though 'does it right' and 'one of the most dependable people on my crew' go a little past the facts given.

works_the_facts.reason: The facts are listed but not worked: it doesn't turn two missed shifts into roughly 2 of about 780, and it leaves out the $8,000 the vet said early detection saved, using the vague 'makes a real difference' in its place.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is the loose 'practical experience that many students won't have', with nothing specific setting him against a typical applicant.

qualification.reason: A reference letter doesn't need hedged conditions, and the document doesn't depend on any.

objections.reason: It handles the written-English worry well with the night class, but it raises the five-week absence without the facts that answer it (his cousin covered his shifts and he returned on the promised date), and it leaves out the part-time weekend job that would answer whether he'll finish the program.

fit.reason: The length and letter format are right for one page, but the farm name, his surname, the manager's name, the phone number and the date are all left as brackets even though the user had given them.
